newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest electricity prices hold mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest electricity prices hold mostly steady.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were mostly steady Wednesday with some warmer temperatures forecast through parts of the area on Thursday, industry brokers and marketers said.
Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), Thursday peak, non-firm power prices were pegged steady at $30.00-33.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP next day power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday were talked higher at $32.00-33.00 from $28.00-30.00 on Tuesday, the brokers and marketers said.
MAIN off peak Thursday power was said to be unchanged at $12.00-14.00 per MWh.
Temperatures in MAIN were expected to moderate to slightly below normal on Thursday with normal temperatures expected on Friday and predictions of colder air over the weekend.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Thursday were said to be discussed at $30.00-31.50 from $26.00-30.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.

In ECAR, Consumers Power Co continued to investigate the cause of a shutdown at its 780 megawatt Palisades nuclear power plant in Michigan and had not set a date for the plant to resume electricity production.
The plant was shut Jan 23 after a problem with electrical equipment at a main generator.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00 per MWh.
February ECAR was assessed steady at $22.80-23.00 per MWh.

Temperatures in ECAR were forecast to run five to 10 degrees below normal on Thursday, then warm slightly on Friday and turn colder again on the weekend with temperatures again five to 10 degrees below normal.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday delivery were pegged lower at $33.00-34.00 from $34.00-35.00 in the north and lower at $25.00-27.00 in the south from $27.00-29.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
Off-peak next day prices throughout SPP were notionally assessed steady at $17.00-19.00 in the north and steady at $13.00-15.00 in the south, the sources said.
February SPP was notionally assessed steady at $23.25-23.90 per MWh.
In SPP, temperatures were expected to be near to slightly below normal through Thursday, then warming on Friday to 10 to 20 degrees above normal by Sunday.
